name: Planning Data public transport access node dataset
fact: Planning Data exposes the Department for Transport NaPTAN access-node inventory; collector last ran 23 July 2026 and new data was found the same day.
gate: Dataset/node presence is a transport-access screen only; it does not prove service frequency, capacity, walkability or parcel connectivity.

name: DfT Connectivity Tool
fact: Department for Transport guidance was updated 3 July 2026; the tool measures relative access to everyday destinations by walking, cycling, public transport and driving, with a registration-free Lite version.
gate: Connectivity scores are relative planning evidence, not a planning permission, service guarantee or parcel development score.

name: Connectivity Tool user manual
fact: The public manual explains the map, glossary and use of the DfT national connectivity metric.
gate: Tool operation guidance does not establish the suitability or deliverability of a development site.

name: Applying Connectivity Tool
fact: DfT says the tool is designed for spatial and transport planning and can help identify sustainable locations and transport interventions.
gate: A connectivity score or intervention scenario is not a transport assessment, funding commitment or planning consent.

name: Interpreting Connectivity Scores
fact: DfT states scores are relative to the highest-scoring location and should not be directly compared across modes or destination types.
gate: Do not convert a 0-100 connectivity score into an absolute accessibility, capacity or viability percentage.

name: DfT local transport plans collection
fact: Published 2 April 2026; statutory guidance covers preparation, implementation and review of local transport plans in England.
gate: An LTP is authority-level policy and programme evidence, not proof a parcel has funded transport infrastructure.

name: DfT local transport plans detailed guidance
fact: The 2026 guidance requires alignment of transport and development and covers accessibility, buses, local roads, carbon and implementation.
gate: Local transport policy must be linked to exact funded schemes and site evidence before affecting parcel readiness.

name: Travel Plans, Transport Assessments and Statements
fact: National guidance says significant transport-generating development may require a Transport Statement or Transport Assessment, judged case by case.
gate: Requirement for assessment is not evidence that transport impacts are acceptable or mitigated.

name: Transport evidence bases in plan making
fact: Guidance requires iterative assessment of accessibility, congestion, network gaps, proposed allocations and transport investment needs during plan making.
gate: Plan-level evidence cannot be promoted to site-specific highway capacity or planning acceptability.

name: How to assess and allocate sites for development
fact: Published 31 March 2026; guidance covers site assessment, allocation-policy drafting and structured site-assessment templates.
gate: Assessment or allocation is not planning permission and transport evidence remains one part of deliverability.

name: DfT Transport Analysis Guidance
fact: Transport Analysis Guidance was updated 28 May 2026 and provides modelling/appraisal guidance for transport investment decisions.
gate: TAG appraisal is investment-analysis evidence and does not by itself establish development-site transport capacity.

name: TAG data book
fact: DfT updated the TAG data book on 28 May 2026 with current appraisal and modelling reference values.
gate: National appraisal parameters are not local measured traffic, service or capacity data.

name: TAG unit M3-1 highway assignment modelling
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; DfT guidance covers highway assignment modelling and model fitness for purpose.
gate: Model outputs require project-specific calibration and cannot be treated as observed junction or road capacity.

name: TAG unit M4 forecasting and uncertainty
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; TAG M4 addresses forecasting and uncertainty in transport appraisal.
gate: Forecast scenarios are not guaranteed traffic demand or infrastructure delivery.

name: TAG unit A3 environmental impact appraisal
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; TAG A3 covers environmental impact analysis for transport appraisal.
gate: Transport environmental appraisal is not a site environmental permit or planning consent.

name: TAG unit A1-3 user and provider impacts
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; TAG A1-3 covers user and provider impacts in transport appraisal.
gate: Appraisal benefits/costs do not establish parcel value uplift or service capacity.

name: TAG unit A2-1 wider economic impacts
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; TAG A2-1 provides the framework for wider economic impacts.
gate: Wider-economic modelling cannot be assigned directly to an individual parcel without a valid project appraisal.

name: TAG unit A1-1 cost-benefit analysis
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; TAG A1-1 sets principles and reporting for transport cost-benefit analysis.
gate: A positive transport business case is not planning permission or guaranteed site value.

name: DfT appraisal, modelling and evaluation strategy
fact: Published 28 May 2026; DfT sets a five-year strategy for transport appraisal, modelling and evaluation methods.
gate: Methodology strategy is not a project-specific transport intervention or funding award.

name: TAG forthcoming changes
fact: Updated 28 May 2026; DfT currently reports no forthcoming TAG changes.
gate: Version status is a methodology control and not evidence for a development site.

name: Government vision for buses
fact: Published 2 April 2026; policy sets expectations for comprehensive, reliable, inclusive and sustainable bus services outside London.
gate: National bus policy does not prove a specific route, stop frequency or funded intervention near a parcel.

name: Bus enhanced partnerships guidance
fact: Current DfT guidance explains enhanced partnerships and their relationship to local transport plans and bus service improvement plans.
gate: An enhanced partnership does not guarantee service frequency or accessibility at a target site.

name: Bus franchising guidance
fact: Updated 29 January 2026; guidance explains statutory and non-statutory processes for bus franchising under current legislation.
gate: A franchising process is authority-level governance evidence, not a site-level service commitment.

name: Bus grant payment scheme guidance
fact: Published 29 January 2026; statutory guidance covers local-authority powers to design and pay bus grants.
gate: Grant powers do not prove funding has been allocated to a route or development.

name: Local Authority Bus Grant allocations
fact: Published 5 December 2025; allocations cover revenue to 2029 and capital to 2030 under the consolidated grant model.
gate: Authority allocation is not evidence that a particular corridor, stop or development will receive investment.

name: Bus services grants and funding collection
fact: DfT collection includes bus grants and funding routes, including the newer Bus Service Operators Grant Plus.
gate: Funding-programme availability is not a project-specific award.

name: Environmental advice for planning proposals
fact: Updated 1 July 2026; cross-agency guidance covers environmental advice for construction and transport developers.
gate: Pre-application advice does not replace planning permission, environmental permits or statutory consents.

name: PINS new-style local plans collection
fact: Published 18 June 2026; PINS collection covers new-style local plans and says the new examination route applies to plans submitted on or after 31 December 2026.
gate: Plan-system procedure is not parcel allocation or permission evidence.

name: Streamlining infrastructure planning implementation plan
fact: Published 23 March 2026; government implementation plan links major infrastructure reform to transport, energy, water and housing delivery.
gate: National implementation targets do not establish consent, timing or benefit for a specific parcel.

name: Launching the Connectivity Tool
fact: The December 2025 ministerial statement describes a national 100m-by-100m connectivity evidence base for England and Wales.
gate: Policy launch context is not a live parcel score and should not replace the current tool outputs.
